newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says stronger bank lending supported Dec M3.
newsitem.headline: Buba says stronger bank lending supported Dec M3.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that stronger bank lending helped support December M3 money supply growth.
In a statement, the central bank said lively domestic private lending and declining monetary capital formation helped December M3 reach a 7.9- percent annualised rate.

This is down only slightly from November's eight-percent rate. The Bundesbank also confirmed that M3 growth for 1996 overshot its four- to seven-percent target growth corridor. In December, sight deposits also grew very strongly.
M3 money supply, a leading policy indicator for the Bundesbank, consists of cash in circulation, and short-term sight, time and savings deposits.
The Bundesbank said domestic non-banks again reduced their holdings in money market funds, which are not included in traditional M3 but are included in so-called extended M3.
The Bundesbank said domestic non-banks allowed their holdings to drop by 400 million marks in December.
Expanded M3 grew at a seasonally adjusted, annualised rate of three percent in the six months from June through November.
One reason sight deposits expanded at an extraordinarily strong rate in December is that companies increased their holidings in sight deposits, the Bundesbank said.

Cash in circulation also showed a clear increase, the Bundesbank said. Short-term time deposits, which had in the past months declined, also expanded. Similarly, savings deposits also increased, the central bank said.

The Bundesbank explained that short-term economic credits, which had grown more slowly in recently months, expanded quite strongly in December. The rate of lending also picked up in longer-term direct loans, the central bank said.

The Bundesbank explained one reason for this may be that tax breaks on new housing stock in eastern Germany expired at the end of 1996 and may have prompted some investors to borrow more heavily late last year.
In the last six months, private sector lending grew at 7.7 percent rate compared with a 5.8 percent in the six months to November, the Bundesbank said.
Meanwhile, monetary capital formation grew at a 4.9 percent rate in the six months to December, down from a rate of 5.2 percent in the six months to November.
